blocks.text: Two Ways to Get a Repository
You either turn an existing directory into a repository with git init, or you copy an existing repository, including its full history, with git clone.

$ mkdir inventory-api && cd inventory-api
$ git init
Initialized empty Git repository in /home/ada/inventory-api/.git/

$ ls -A .git
HEAD  config  description  hooks  info  objects  refs

rows: Points to the current branch (for example ref: refs/heads/main)
The object database: every commit, tree and file content
The staging area (created on the first git add)
Scripts Git can run on events such as pre-commit
Repository-local ignore rules that are not shared

blocks.text: The .git directory is the repository. Your project files are only a checkout of one version of it. Deleting .git deletes all history; copying .git copies all history. Never run git init inside another repository by accident (for example in your home directory), because every file under it becomes an untracked candidate.

git init --bare creates a repository with no working tree: the contents of .git sit directly in the directory, conventionally named project.git. Servers use bare repositories, because nobody edits files there and pushing into a checked-out branch of a non-bare repository would leave its working tree out of sync. GitHub stores your repositories as bare repositories.

# HTTPS: authenticate with a credential manager or personal access token
$ git clone https://github.com/acme/inventory-api.git

# SSH: authenticate with an SSH key
$ git clone git@github.com:acme/inventory-api.git

# Clone into a different directory name
$ git clone git@github.com:acme/inventory-api.git api
git clone is a composite command. Understanding its steps explains the state you end up in:

items: Create the target directory and run git init inside it.
Add a remote named origin pointing to the source URL.
Fetch all branches and tags, creating remote-tracking branches such as origin/main.
Create a local branch matching the remote's default branch, configured to track origin/main.
Check out that branch into the working tree.

blocks.text: Clone Options You Will Meet in Practice

rows: Check out a specific branch or tag after cloning
Shallow clone: only the latest commit
CI jobs that only need to build current code
Partial clone: full history, file contents downloaded on demand
Very large repositories where you still need log and blame

blocks.text: Shallow clones break anything that needs history: git describe, changelog generation, git blame on old lines, and computing which files changed since the base branch. This is why actions/checkout in GitHub Actions defaults to depth 1 and you sometimes need fetch-depth: 0. You will use this in Module 6.
Publishing an Existing Local Project to GitHub

# 1. Create an empty repository on GitHub (no README, so histories do not diverge)
# 2. Connect and push
$ git remote add origin git@github.com:acme/inventory-api.git
$ git branch -M main
$ git push -u origin main
The -u (--set-upstream) flag records origin/main as the upstream of your local main, so later a plain git push or git pull knows where to go. Remotes are covered in depth in Module 3.
